items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: And, uh, he got back to St. Louis. He had his own band. And, uh, he said for me to come up there, but I didn't go that time.

ctx.x: Did they have your name up? You know, did they advertise you were playing there as guest artist? No. No.

No, they didn't even advertise. Not as I can remember. But anyway, uh, this guy, Charlie Crest was playing, uh, accordion with Faith, the us at that time. And, uh, he got back to St. Louis. He had his own band. And, uh, he said for me to come up there, but I didn't go that time. Uh, because I had too much work in the owners. I couldn't leave. I mean, I had too many contracts signed. I couldn't leave. So, uh, so about six, eight months after he come down here, with Faith again, and the farm and then told me he had…
What did you, uh, you got any questions?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: Charlie Chris. Used to work with, with Faith Morgan. He played trumpet and he played, uh, the accordion.

ctx.x: Well, it's his daddy then. That's what I wanted to get straight.

Yeah, his daddy. Uh-huh. Uh. Well, after I left, uh, Pelican, I left here and went to St. Louis. Worked at the Democratic Club there. Uh-huh. Under a fellow by the name of Hawkins. At the Democratic Club at that time. My Bobby Gordon up there, it was through our, uh, Charlie Chris. Used to work with, with Faith Morgan. He played trumpet and he played, uh, the accordion. Oh. He's dead now, a fellow. Uh, up there I had, uh, I can't remember this guy's name. I don't remember one man's name up there. Was playing with…
